subject: Panopticon - production latency & error surge / exec coordination
messages:
From: Sanjay Rao <sanjay.rao@panopticon.ai>
To: hannah_schmitt@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 22 Mar 2028 08:14:00 -0700
Subject: Production: sudden error spike & latency (US-west)

Team —

We're seeing a sudden degradation in our production inference service since ~07:55 PT. Topline symptoms:
- Error rate (5xx) jumped from ~0.2% to 6.1% in the last 20 minutes.
- Median p95 latency is 2.5x normal (p95 went from 420ms to 1.1s).
- Throughput for key endpoints has dropped ~38% for customers routed through us-west-2.

Attached is a telemetry snapshot and a short timeline (telemetry_snapshot_20280322.zip). We rolled no new model versions from our side. We need immediate help — can you confirm impact, an ETA for mitigation, and whether you can put an exec-level war-room for this?

Sanjay
Sanjay Rao
Head of Platform
Panopticon AI

----
Attachment: telemetry_snapshot_20280322.zip (telemetry + partial spans)

From: hannah_schmitt@redwood.com
To: Sanjay Rao <sanjay.rao@panopticon.ai>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com, marcus_lin@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 22 Mar 2028 08:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Production: sudden error spike & latency (US-west)

Thanks Sanjay — we see the same signals in our telemetry. I'm escalating now.

Immediate plan (first 30 min):
- Open a dedicated incident bridge (joining link in Drive).
- Roll traffic away from the affected GPU pool to warm standby (us-west-2-b).
- Temporarily lower batch size on the hr-heavy routes to limit KV cache churn.
- Marcus to validate any recent config pushes that could affect batching/cache.

Vivek / Marcus / Laura — can you join a quick exec sync at 08:40 PT? I will share a draft customer comms after we lock the action plan.

Hannah Schmitt
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

----

From: laura_bennett@redwood.com
To: hannah_schmitt@redwood.com, marcus_lin@redwood.com
Cc: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com, Sanjay Rao <sanjay.rao@panopticon.ai>
Date: Thu, 22 Mar 2028 08:28:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Production: sudden error spike & latency (US-west)

On it — ran a quick diff against the last three config rolls. No model change, but there was a batching-policy tweak pushed at 07:38 PT that increases max_sequence_per_batch for the low-latency tier. That could explain higher memory pressure and KV evictions.

I've exported a short diagnostic-summary.csv with top error stacks and span examples; attaching. If we can temporarily revert the batching-policy or force a smaller batch-size, that should reduce eviction churn.

Also: recommend we pre-authorize a 10% billing credit for impacted windows so we can communicate immediately. Vivek — can you confirm?

Laura Bennett
Senior Customer Success Manager
Redwood Inference

----
Attachment: diagnostic-summary.csv

From: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com
To: hannah_schmitt@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com, marcus_lin@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 22 Mar 2028 08:33:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Production: sudden error spike & latency (US-west)

Appreciate the quick detection. I'm authorizing an exec-level bridge and temporary credit authorization — Laura, please prepare the wording (10% for the impacted window) and include finance in the loop if Panopticon wants an invoice-level adjustment.

We need a short commander log and a single source-of-truth doc. Hannah — spin up the bridge and put the timeline in Drive. Marcus, prioritize validation and rollback plan; if the fix is a config revert, prefer that over code changes.

Vivek Kulkarni
VP, Customer Operations
Redwood Inference

----

From: hannah_schmitt@redwood.com
To: Sanjay Rao <sanjay.rao@panopticon.ai>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com, marcus_lin@redwood.com, finance@panopticon.ai
Date: Thu, 22 Mar 2028 08:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Customer update (draft) — Panopticon impact and next steps

Hi Sanjay / Priya —

We opened an incident bridge at 08:25 PT and have an exec-level team actively working the issue. Key points for your customers:

- What happened: We detected and are mitigating a surge in error rates and latency affecting tenants routed through the us-west-2 GPU pool. Early telemetry points to increased KV cache eviction driven by batching-policy changes.
- What we're doing: shifting traffic to warm standby capacity, temporarily reducing batch sizes on heavy routes, and preparing a safe config rollback for the batching policy.
- ETA: attempting mitigation now with an operational ETA of 45 minutes to restore normal p95 and error-rate ranges. We'll confirm as soon as the rollback completes.
- Credits: we will pre-authorize a 10% credit for the impacted window; your finance contact is CC'd.

Next steps: we will provide a stamped timeline, root-cause analysis, and a remediation plan within 24 hours.

If this looks good, we'll send this to customers in the impacted segment and post a status update to your status page if you want us to.

Thanks —
Hannah

----
Attachment: draft_customer_update.md

From: marcus_lin@redwood.com
To: hannah_schmitt@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com
Cc: Sanjay Rao <sanjay.rao@panopticon.ai>
Date: Thu, 22 Mar 2028 08:59:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Production: sudden error spike & latency (US-west)

Short technical update:
- Root cause: suspected KV cache churn caused by the 07:38 batching-policy tweak that increases max_sequence_per_batch. Under a burst profile this increases resident memory and triggers eviction loops, which in turn surfaces 5xxs and latency.
- Mitigation prepared: config revert + force-smaller-batch override for the low-latency tier. Rolling to canary nodes now (us-west-2-a subset).
- Rollback plan: if canary passes in 10 minutes, we will roll to the remaining nodes with 5-minute watch windows. If anything regresses, we will re-route to standby pool and keep canary at small batch size.
- ETA: 45 minutes to full restoration if rollback goes as planned.

I'll post live logs to the Drive folder; attaching a short timeline CSV.

Marcus Lin
Head of Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

----
Attachment: diagnostic-timeline.csv

From: Sanjay Rao <sanjay.rao@panopticon.ai>
To: hannah_schmitt@redwood.com
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com, marcus_lin@redwood.com, finance@panopticon.ai
Date: Thu, 22 Mar 2028 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Production: sudden error spike & latency (US-west)

Thanks everyone — that plan sounds good. Please proceed with the config revert and routing to warm standby. We appreciate the proactive credit authorization; finance will follow up with Laura.

Two asks from our side:
1) Please publish a stamped timeline once the rollback is complete so we can share with our internal stakeholders.
2) After stabilization, request a 30-minute post-mortem tomorrow with both teams to go over root cause and verify the rollback doesn't hide systemic risk.

I'll standby on the bridge.

Sanjay
